brief.situation: 15:00 in an outpatient pelvic health clinic. You are the physical therapist. Ms. Adeyemi, 31, was referred for bladder training. She has had urgency, frequency, nocturia and urge leakage for 6 weeks.
handover: She mentions that last year she 'lost the vision in my right eye for a few weeks, with pain moving it', which got better on its own.
Clinic policy: urinary symptoms with new neurological signs go back to the referring provider the same day for neurology referral; pelvic floor care can continue alongside.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: What is driving her urge incontinence?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: Urge incontinence can come from detrusor overactivity or neurological disease; leg sensory symptoms, brisk reflexes, bilateral Babinski and a past painful vision loss suggest a demyelinating disease such as MS, in which bladder problems are common.
parts.modelAnswer: Probably neurological. Her legs are numb, her reflexes are brisk with upgoing toes, and she had what sounds like optic neuritis. MS often causes bladder urgency.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Calls the provider the same day for neurology and MRI, continues pelvic floor care with a bladder diary and urge strategies, documents.
parts.modelAnswer: Call her provider today for neurology and an MRI, keep the bladder diary and urge strategies going, and document it.

scoring.modelReasoning: Urge incontinence (frequency, urgency, nocturia) comes from detrusor overactivity or from neurological disease such as stroke, Parkinson disease or multiple sclerosis. Screen neurologically: Ms. Adeyemi's leg sensory symptoms, brisk reflexes, bilateral Babinski signs and past painful monocular vision loss suggest MS, in which bladder problems are common, and relapsing-remitting MS is the first course in about 85%. Refer for neurology the same day and continue pelvic floor care alongside.
